dedupe_keys.name: usgs community exposure to coastal hazards hera hazard exposure reporting and analytics

description: These USGS data releases estimate how many people, jobs, buildings, land and infrastructure assets in U.S. coastal communities lie in zones exposed to coastal flooding, groundwater rise and shoreline change under present and future sea level rise and storm scenarios. They are produced by the U.S. Geological Survey's Western Geographic Science Center, led by Jeanne M. Jones and Nathan J. Wood, and generated with the Hazard Exposure Reporting and Analytics (HERA) web application, which combines hazard zones from USGS coastal models such as CoSMoS with socioeconomic layers. Indicators include census counts of residents by type, employees by sector, county parcel values, building replacement values, land cover, and roads, rail and critical facilities. Coverage: releases for California, Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, Washington, Hawaii and the Pacific territories (2016 to 2023). Access: CSV tables with a data dictionary on ScienceBase for each state, and interactive maps in HERA. Licence: U.S. federal data in the public domain; free. Caveats: exposure, not damage, and results depend on each hazard model and on commercial employment data. Simulation uses are coastal adaptation planning, prioritising critical facilities at risk and scenario comparison of sea level rise. Related records: HIFLD and the U.S. national structure inventory.
